note: The image both platforms build from the same recipe, and the patched Quartz inside it. Neither app can change these — the launchers build the image from `Dockerfile`, `patches/` and `scripts/`, and tag it by a hash of that whole context. It is in the contract because both sides must know WHY each pin is where it is: a version raised for a good local reason can break every teacher's site build, and the reasons are not visible from the version numbers.

patches.cannotBeDropped: Without it a course either publishes what a teacher hid, or hides most of itself.
patches.does: Decides page visibility from `publish:`, defaulting to VISIBLE.
patches.whyNotStock: Quartz ships two filters and neither says what a teacher means. RemoveDrafts publishes everything except `draft: true` — the word reads as 'unfinished' rather than 'students cannot see it', and the polarity is backwards from how teachers talk. ExplicitPublish publishes only `publish: true` — the right word, but it flips the default: in the example course 60 of 225 pages carry no flag at all, including every curriculum page, and every one would silently vanish.

patches.cannotBeDropped: publish.ts is not reachable without it.
patches.does: Exports the filter above in place of the stock pair.

patches.cannotBeDropped: The teacher's own choices in the settings form stop reaching the site.
patches.does: Reads `expandable` and `expandOnFolderClick` from course_config.json, sorts the tree the way a course reads, and passes both to the client script.

patches.cannotBeDropped: The server-rendered attributes are read by nothing.
patches.does: The client half of the same: which folders expand, and what a click on one does.

patches.cannotBeDropped: Folder landing pages revert to Quartz's own listing.
patches.does: What a folder's own page shows.

patches.cannotBeDropped: Two things go at once. Social preview tags point to Jacky Zhao's domain when baseUrl is empty or unconfigured, AND every page falls back to the stock <link rel="icon" href="static/icon.png">, so each of a teacher's class sites wears the Quartz logo in the browser tab.
patches.does: Constructs OpenGraph and Twitter meta tags using the section's baseUrl when present, or page-relative paths when absent, rather than defaulting to quartz.jzhao.xyz. Also replaces the single stock favicon link with three page-relative ones — static/favicon.ico (sizes=32x32), static/icon.svg (type=image/svg+xml) and apple-touch-icon pointing at static/apple-touch-icon.png — in that ORDER, because a browser takes the last icon it understands, so the .ico serves older Safari and Windows shortcuts while the SVG wins wherever it is supported. The files themselves are installed by build_site.py from support/favicon.
patches.whyNotStock: Stock Quartz unconditionally constructs og:image as https://${cfg.baseUrl}/static/og-image.png, which points to Jacky Zhao's site when baseUrl defaults to quartz.jzhao.xyz and generates invalid URLs when baseUrl is empty. The patch falls back to page-relative static/og-image.png when baseUrl is not configured. Stock Quartz also links its own quartz/static/icon.png as the favicon; the patch links Plantoir's icon set instead. If Head.tsx is ever re-derived against a newer Quartz, BOTH behaviours have to come with it — the favicon links are the half with no visible symptom during development, because a local preview looks identical either way.

patches.cannotBeDropped: Without it fast rebuilds and quick retries fail with ENOTEMPTY errors on bind-mounted host filesystems.
patches.does: Cleans the output directory with retries and recursive fallback instead of crashing when rimraf encounters pending host directory unlinks.
patches.whyNotStock: Stock Quartz calls rimraf with a wildcard glob that crashes on virtiofs/Docker bind mounts with ENOTEMPTY when removing subdirectories. The patch adds retry options and a recursive fs.rm fallback.

pins.why: Python for the build scripts, with Node added on top. The site build is Node; the pipeline around it is Python.

#640 (v1.9.0): Node 22.23.4 from NodeSource (`setup_22.x`), PINNED EXACTLY. Node 20 has been end-of-life since 2026-04-30, and the unpinned `setup_20.x` let the image and Windows' runtime drift to different patch releases (#636). 22.23.4 is the 2026-10-20 security release (npm 10.9.9, OpenSSL 3.5.9). An `=` pin is safe here, unlike caCertificates' floor: NodeSource keeps its history (measured 2026-10-23: every 22.x from 22.5.0 on arm64, 22.23.4 and back past 22.22.0 on amd64), so the pin does not break a first build the day 22.23.5 ships. Quartz v4.5.0 is still what decides this, and was revalidated on 22: an identical `npm ls --all` tree for Quartz and the tikz engine (665 lines, no EBADENGINE), byte-identical figure-cache SVG, the same 336 files for the EXC2O example with 0 differences once timestamps and Explorer ids are set aside, and verify.sh and verify-deploy.sh green. The one new behaviour, a `punycode` DEP0040 deprecation line on every Quartz build, is silenced by build_site.py (`--disable-warning=DEP0040`, that one warning only). Node's own built-in store (`tls.rootCertificates`) holds 116 roots and neither caCertificates subject; verify.sh checks the version, wrangler's engines and that store. Node 22 is end-of-life on 2027-04-30, so Quartz 5 (#512) or Node 24 must land before then. Windows' runtime carries the same 22.23.4 since #675 (v1.9.0; fetch-runtime.ps1's `$NodeVersion`, held to this pin by windowsRuntimeContains, five spaces and all), so both platforms run one Node; there, global `WebSocket` exists without `--experimental-websocket` and Quartz's `npm ls --all` tree is the one it had on 20.18.1. REJECTED: Node 24 (the ruling on #636 is 22, and 24 is a second, unmeasured jump); a floating `setup_22.x` (#636's drift again); a late `nodejs` layer over Node 20 (saves existing teachers about 90 MB, estimated, but every npm layer below must rebuild anyway, Node 20's files stay as dead weight, and no no-cache build reproduces the image).

Cloudflare's own deploy CLI, used by `deploy.py` for the Pages destination. PINNED EXACTLY at the newest 4.x on 2026-10-31 (#699, `npm view wrangler dist-tags.latest`, published 2026-10-29): the exact pin keeps the image reproducible and stops an upstream CLI change from breaking publishing for a teacher mid-semester. It was held at 4.80.0 by a `mustStayBelow` of 4.87, the first wrangler whose `engines.node` is `>=22.0.0`, until both platforms ran Node 22.23.4 (the image since #640, Windows' runtime since #675); this move RETIRED that ceiling on both platforms, and with it the mac's and Windows' tests of it. `nodeEngine` is wrangler's own `engines.node` at this pin: verify.sh reads it from the image's wrangler package.json, and the mac suite checks the `node` pin satisfies it - the invariant that matters from now on. `windowsRuntimeContains` is fetch-runtime.ps1's own line, so the two platforms' wranglers cannot drift apart quietly again. Why it moved (#699): 4.156.0's own wrangler-dist/cli.js BUNDLES undici 7.30.1 (4.80.0 bundled 7.24.4), and npm audit finds NO advisory in its tree, against 35 in 4.80.0's (the four wrangler entries in npmAudit.accepted went stale and were deleted). MEASURED for `pages deploy` (#712's transcripts, research/wrangler/): its options are unchanged, new global flags are off by default, and the success line is still `Uploaded N files`. NEW since 4.108, and the one behaviour to know: when wrangler believes an AI agent is driving it (CLAUDECODE, AI_AGENT and others in its environment, or an agent among its ancestors), a deploy that would CREATE a new static project goes to Cloudflare Workers instead of Pages. deploy.py is guarded three ways: it passes `--branch`, an argument that delegation refuses; `ensure_pages_project` makes the project through the API before wrangler runs; and on the mac `docker exec` hands the container six named variables only. verify-deploy.sh fails a Cloudflare leg that prints the delegation's notice. REJECTED: a version below 4.120, to keep a miniflare 5 pre-release out of the tree (`pages deploy` never starts miniflare, and the ruling was the newest 4.x on the day); a range instead of an exact pin; waiting for wrangler 5.
The site generator, cloned at a tag. The patches below are written against this version; a newer Quartz means re-deriving all seven.

Reads and REWRITES every page's frontmatter in `build_site.process_frontmatter`, which is what decides whether a teacher's page reaches their students. Pinned 2026-09-18 with issue #140, at the version the image already had — the pin changes nothing about what is installed and everything about what can change underneath it.

**The pin that decides what a teacher's `publish:` line MEANS.** python-frontmatter parses with PyYAML, which is YAML **1.1** — and that is the only reason `publish: no` and `publish: off` hide a page. PyYAML 7 is expected to move to YAML 1.2, where `no` is the string "no" and every such page would be PUBLISHED, silently, in courses already in front of students. `contracts/file-formats.json` -> `pageVisibility` states the 1.1 table as fact and both apps are written against it, so an unpinned upgrade would fail nothing anywhere. Named explicitly rather than left to python-frontmatter's own dependency range, because that range is not ours to control.

Draws each section's social sharing card. Pinned with the other two rather than for a known break: an unpinned image is not reproducible, and a card that renders differently is a thing teachers notice after the fact. Its FreeType decodes WOFF2 fonts with Brotli carriesBrotli (the image: pillow.libs/libbrotlidec-*.so.1.2.0, a shared library; Windows: linked into _imagingft, the wheel's LICENSE says brotli-1.2.0), which CVE-2026-111497 affects (1.0.3 to 1.2.0, fixed in brotliFixedFrom). Kept at 12.3.0 (#766, Russell 2026-11-12) because no Pillow release carries 1.2.1 yet (13.0.0 still has 1.2.0) and the decoder only reads the TrueType fonts shared-rules.json -> socialCardFonts lists. Move when a release's .github/dependencies.json says brotli 1.2.1 or later, and update carriesBrotli: verify.sh fails on the image the day the two disagree.

The print layout for pages whose settings say printable: true (#454): it paginates the handout in the page itself, so the school name, the blanks and 'Page 1 of 3' print in the corners in every browser, Safari included, which prints no margin boxes of its own. Carried at /opt/vendor/pagedjs (Windows: runtime\vendor\pagedjs) and copied into a section's site ONLY when a page students can see opts in - dist/paged.min.js is 502,617 bytes (96,934 gzipped), so a course that never prints carries none of it. The UMD global is `PagedModule` (not `Paged`). MIT. A QUIET project, which is the risk to know: 0.4.3 has been npm's latest since 2023-07-06, with only 0.5.0-beta.2 (2024-10-04) since, so a browser change it does not keep up with is ours to work around. `sha256` is the tarball's, which the recipe checks; `fileSha256` is paged.min.js's, which verify.sh checks in the image.

#499 (v1.6.0), Debian 13's fonts-lmodern 2.005-1 (apt names no version, so a point release cannot fail a build): the faces a printed handout is set in, so it reads like the teacher's LaTeX handouts (11pt article with lmodern): Latin Modern Roman regular, bold, italic and bold italic, Sans bold, Mono. Carried at /opt/vendor/pagedjs/fonts (Windows: runtime\vendor\pagedjs\fonts since #503's batch 5A, 2026-10-15 - unpacked by fetch-runtime.ps1 from the same Debian package, fonts-lmodern_2.005-1_all.deb, checked by its own SHA-256 and each font against `files`; `windowsRuntimeContains` names that file and is read only by the Windows suite, nothing on the mac reads it) beside Paged.js, so a site carries them only when a page students can see opts in to printing, and a browser fetches them only when a page is printed: 631,940 bytes, unmodified OTF. From Debian's fonts-lmodern through apt, not from GUST's download page, because a font host that is down must never fail a teacher's first build; `files` are the SHA-256s verify.sh checks in the image. GUST Font License (an instance of the LPPL 1.3c), which asks that a CHANGED font be renamed - so the files are not converted to woff2 (283,148 bytes for the six, measured with fontTools 4) and keep their own names. REJECTED: KaTeX's Computer Modern from the CDN (no bytes, but it needs the network at the moment of printing and has no sans or mono for headings and code); the GUST zip pinned by hash (lm2.004otf.zip, 3,907,819 bytes - a second network host for every first build).

#485 E1: draws a page's ```functionplot graphs in the student's browser, and checks each one at build time with the same file (its evaluator, $eval.builtIn) so a graph the site would refuse is reported to the teacher first. Carried at /opt/vendor/function-plot (Windows: runtime\vendor\function-plot) and copied into a section's site ONLY when a page students can see has a graph that can be drawn - dist/function-plot.js is 202,953 bytes (60,012 gzipped), MIT. The Obsidian functionplot plugin 1.2.1 bundles function-plot ^1.22.9; 1.25.4 is the same evaluator family (`log` is natural, `log10`, `PI`, `E`, `2x` work; `ln`, `pi`, `x**2` do not - figureFences.functionplot.expressionCases). It evaluates with `new Function`, which the Netlify header's 'unsafe-eval' already allows. The bundle names `self` as it loads, so the build's helper sets `globalThis.self` first. `sha256` is the tarball's, which the recipe checks; `fileSha256` is function-plot.js's, which verify.sh checks in the image and in a built site.

#485 E1: draws a page's ```tikz diagrams at BUILD time, so students download no engine (the Obsidian plugin's browser engine is 7.0 MB of script plus 4.8 MB of fonts). Its TeX engine - tex.wasm, core.dump and all 212 TeX files - is byte-identical to the one obsidian-tikzjax 0.5.2 embeds (measured by SHA-256 of each decompressed file, 213 distinct contents on each side, none on one side only), so a fence draws the same picture in Obsidian and on the site; the JavaScript AROUND the engine differs (@prinsss/dvi2html 0.0.1 and svgo 3.3.5 against the plugin's own dvi2html and svgo 2), so 'same picture' also rests on four diagrams compared by viewBox and text runs. Installed with `npm ci --omit=dev` from support/figures/package-lock.json, which pins all 133 packages under it - load-bearing, because node-tikzjax floats jsdom ^23, svgo ^3 and memfs ^4 and svgo shapes every drawing; the lockfile is also part of the figure cache's engine id (figureFences.cache), so a moved package draws every diagram afresh. 39 MB of files, 5,445 of them, 14.4 MB compressed; carried at /opt/vendor/tikz-engine (Windows: runtime\vendor\tikz-engine) and NEVER copied into a site - a site carries only the Computer Modern faces its diagrams use (static/tikz). LPPL-1.3c (node-tikzjax, TikZJax); the 212 TeX files carry their own LPPL and GPL terms; the BaKoMa faces their own licence - THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md. `sha256` is the npm tarball's, for the record (the lockfile's integrity line is what npm checks); `files` are the engine's own three, which verify.sh checks in the image. REJECTED: TikZJax in the browser (4.94 MB gzipped per student, 1.8 s for four diagrams); installing into Quartz's node_modules; bundling it with esbuild (it reads tex/ beside itself); a fork without jsdom.

CARRIED, not fetched when a site is built (Russell, 2026-10-05): the core tarball (6,757,104 bytes, `sha256`) is downloaded once into the image and checked; five of its files are kept, 13,531,207 bytes (pyodide.mjs 17,931; pyodide.asm.mjs 1,250,344; pyodide.asm.wasm 9,598,218; python_stdlib.zip 2,545,637; pyodide-lock.json 119,077), at /opt/vendor/pyodide (Windows: runtime\vendor\pyodide) with a README naming MPL-2.0 (the tarball carries no LICENSE file). A site carries them, with support/gated/pyodide/plantoir-worker.js, only when a page students can see has a runnable block (codeRunnerBlocks.siteCarriesEngine). pyodide.mjs, not pyodide.js (#455 review B1: Pyodide 314 refuses a classic worker wherever data: scripts are allowed), and pyodide.asm.mjs, not .asm.js. pyodide.mjs names one other address, a jsdelivr fallback for packages; the worker pins indexURL, packageBaseUrl and cdnUrl to the site's own folder, so it is never used, and verify.sh allows exactly that one string. #494: the KaTeX a site's maths is styled and copied with, served by the site itself (static/katex/) instead of cdn.jsdelivr.net. Quartz v4.5.0's lockfile installs katex 0.16.21 (rehype-katex 7.0.1 renders every formula with it at build time), but its latex.ts linked 0.16.11's stylesheet and copy-tex from the CDN on every page - so sites rendered with one version and styled with another. Copied from Quartz's own node_modules on every build (build_site.install_katex_assets): katex.min.css (23,352 bytes), contrib/copy-tex.min.js (1,673), the 20 woff2 faces (259,792) and the LICENSE (MIT) - 284,817 bytes plus the licence on EVERY site, because Python cannot tell maths the way remark-math does and a wrong guess breaks every formula silently. woff2 only: every browser that can run a site's code (module workers: Safari 15+) takes woff2 first and never asks for woff or ttf. `npm ls katex@0.16.21` after Quartz's npm install fails the image build if the lockfile ever resolves another version (measured: 0.16.22 exits 1). No windowsRuntimeContains: Windows' runtime takes the same lockfile; documentation/12-windows-app.md records the version it measures. REJECTED: gating per site on maths; all three font formats (1.10 MB); inlining the CSS into index.css; absolute /static/katex/ links (break a folder published under a subpath).

#639 (v1.9.0): Debian's certificate store, at least this version - the one that stops trusting `mustNotTrust`, the Comodo and eMudhra roots above the intermediates compromised in October 2026. Python's urllib trusts this store (its default paths lead to /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt), and urllib is every Netlify publish and deploy.py's own Cloudflare calls; OpenSSL checks no revocation, so distrusting the roots is the protection. A FLOOR (`dpkg --compare-versions ... ge`) in a late layer (since #714 the layer that takes all of trixie-security's upgrades), not an `=` pin: Debian's security archive serves only its newest version, so an exact pin breaks every first build the day deb13u2 ships, and a later version only distrusts more. verify.sh checks the version, that neither subject is in the bundle, in Python's default context or in the hashed certificate folder, and that the store still holds more than 100 certificates, so an empty store cannot pass. Debian removed exactly these two: emSign Root CA - G1, emSign Root CA - C1 and emSign ECC Root CA - C3 (also eMudhra) stay trusted, which is Debian's choice and not ours to curate. Measured 2026-10-23: 150 certificates at 20250419, 148 at this version. No windowsRuntimeContains: Windows' Python reads the Windows certificate stores, not this file. Node's own built-in store (`tls.rootCertificates`, which wrangler uses) is not this file either: measured by #640, Node 22.23.4's holds 116 roots and neither subject, and of the four emSign roots Node 20.20.2's held (144 roots) it keeps only emSign Root CA - G1, as Debian does; verify.sh checks it under the `node` pin. REJECTED: an exact pin; a base-digest bump (a full rebuild for every teacher, and it moves Python's patch release); `apt-get upgrade` (unbounded: #714 measured it at 25 packages and found it would move nodejs off its exact pin; the security layer it shares with libbrotli1 and libssl3t64 takes trixie-security's upgrades only); snapshot.debian.org (a new dependency on a first build); the main apt line (~330 MB again for every teacher who has built); trusting NodeSource's setup script, which happens to install ca-certificates, to keep doing so - and a cached layer never re-runs it.

#714 (v1.9.1): Debian's Brotli decoder, at least this version - the one that fixes CVE-2026-111497 (Node2Shell, in CISA's KEV since 2026-10-27). curl links it (`libbrotlidec.so.1`), and curl runs only at build time here - every download in the build (NodeSource's setup, Paged.js, function-plot and Pyodide above this layer, GeoGebra after it; on a cached Mac those above it ran once, on b7) - and never passes `--compressed`, so the exposure was small; but the image was the one place Plantoir shipped the decoder unpatched. The base (frozen by its digest) has no libbrotli1; it arrives with curl on the main apt line, so a cached Mac kept 1.1.0-2+b7. Node's own bundled Brotli is a separate copy and is fixed in Node 22.23.4 (the `node` pin). A FLOOR (`dpkg --compare-versions ... ge`) in the late security layer, not an `=` pin, for the certificate store's reason: Debian's security archive serves only its newest version. The Dockerfile names it explicitly beside the security selector, so its candidate is taken from whichever archive has it. `debianPackage` makes verify.sh check the installed version against `value`. No windowsRuntimeContains: Windows' Python and Node carry no separate libbrotli. REJECTED: a full `apt-get upgrade` (it would move nodejs off its exact pin the day NodeSource ships 22.23.5); an exact pin; a base-digest bump (a full rebuild for every teacher, and it moves Python's patch release).

#714 (v1.9.1): Debian's OpenSSL library, at least this version (3.5.7; the image carried 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, about 14 CVEs older per Debian's security tracker on 2026-10-31). Python's `_ssl` links it - `ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION` read 3.5.6 before this layer and 3.5.7 after - so it is the TLS under every Netlify publish and deploy.py's own Cloudflare calls, and curl links it too. Node's TLS is its own bundled OpenSSL, under the `node` pin. Found while fixing libbrotli1: #714 first said openssl matched trixie-security, which was not true by 2026-10-31. 3.5.7 is in BOTH trixie-security (deb13u3) and the 13.7 point release (deb13u2), which is why the Dockerfile names libssl3t64 and openssl explicitly beside the Debian-Security selector: a newer stable-only version would otherwise leave it at the base's copy and fail this floor on every first build. A FLOOR in the late security layer, as caCertificates and libbrotli1; `debianPackage` makes verify.sh check it. No windowsRuntimeContains: Windows' Python ships its own OpenSSL with python.org's build. REJECTED: as libbrotli1.

#578: GeoGebra sketches students can drag on a class site (shared-rules.json -> geogebraFences, from stage 2). GeoGebra Math Apps 5.4.933.1 (the zip `sha256`, 33,461,640 bytes, Last-Modified 2026-10-19) is downloaded once into the image by the Dockerfile and checked; scripts/geogebra_engine.py `adapt` - the ONE recipe, which Windows' fetch-runtime.ps1 runs too, into runtime\vendor\geogebra - keeps deployggb.js, HTML5/5.0/css/ and the web3d codebase (it serves classic, graphing, geometry and 3d, measured in Chromium and WebKit), leaves out the 83 language files (web3d/js/properties_keys_*.js, 23 MB; English is built in, and a missing language falls back to it), web3d/html/, sworker-locked.js, web3d.nocache.mjs, and the web/, webSimple/ and GeoGebra.html copies, and writes a README.txt: `fileCount` files, `bytes` bytes (8.95 MB gzipped), at /opt/vendor/geogebra. A site carries them (static/geogebra) only while a page students can see has a sketch (page_features.GATED_ASSETS). SIX exact string replacements (geogebra_engine.REPLACEMENTS), each required to match exactly once or the step refuses and writes nothing: under the Netlify policy a published site is sent (script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' <hashes>, netlify_badge.py) the stock engine NEVER loads, in Chromium or WebKit, because GWT's loader injects its main file and deferred fragments as inline script text (on any host but 127.0.0.1, localhost and apps-builds.), nine resources go into <head> as inline scripts, and its zip library starts a blob: worker; the replacements make each a same-origin <script src> or an eval, and put the loader's hidden frame under <html>, because Quartz's page navigation replaces <body> and took the frame with it (Chromium then loaded no second sketch until a reload). `files` are the three files those replacements touch or a page loads first, hashed AFTER all six (only web3d.nocache.js carries the frame fix; the cache.js hash is the same with or without it), checked in the image by verify.sh. Licence (https://www.geogebra.org/license, updated Nov 2025): free to use for NON-COMMERCIAL purposes with the notice 'Made with GeoGebra(R)' linked to https://www.geogebra.org; language and interface files CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The six replacements and their redistribution rest on the EUPL 1.2, the licence of GeoGebra's source code (which the two changed files are), with a notice of what changed and a pointer to https://github.com/geogebra/geogebra in README.txt - NOT on the non-commercial grant's 'copy, distribute, modify', which is the clause for GeoGebra's Materials (stage-1 review); the engine used with its style and interface files stays non-commercial. It is free while Plantoir is free: if Plantoir is ever sold, contact office@geogebra.org FIRST. Redistributed in three places, all permitted non-commercially: the plantoir.app mirror, the Windows installer, every class site. THE DOWNLOAD HOST IS FLAKY: 4 of 8 connections to download.geogebra.org timed out (2026-10-23, about 20:35 EDT), and guessed older version URLs 404, so a pinned version may vanish upstream. Hence `urls`: the Dockerfile retries the first (download.geogebra.org) six times, then fetches the SAME zip from plantoir.app's mirror, and checks the same SHA-256 whichever answered. The mirror is filled by website/build.py from a cache outside the repository and is never committed; website/build.py --deploy refuses while it is missing or its SHA-256 is not this one, and --verify-deploy fetches it back (RELEASING.md). REJECTED: widening the site's policy (worker-src blob: alone is not enough; the inline scripts need 'unsafe-inline', which the hashes disable and which would let Netlify's badge back in); pinning about ten inline hashes (fonts vary, and one missed hash is broken lettering, silently); a run-time patch of head.appendChild (it cannot reach the first two, which run in GWT's frame before any of our code); loading GeoGebra from geogebra.org (a third party on every page, and blocked by the same policy); `material_id` in deployggb (it calls geogebra.org); committing the zip or the mirror (33.5 MB in every clone, and every bump kept in history); the web or webSimple codebase (no 3D, or no toolbar and algebra view).

rules.detail: Every file in `Dockerfile`, `patches/`, `scripts/`, `support/`, `contracts/` and the launchers. `contracts/` joined the context when the scripts themselves began reading the contract: the container's only bind mount is `courses`, so a shared rule it cannot see is no rule at all. The cost is accepted deliberately — a contract edit changes the hash and forces a rebuild.
rules.rule: The image tag is a HASH of the whole build context
rules.why: A changed recipe means a new tag, a rebuild and a recreated container — with no update checks anywhere, and no way for a teacher to be running a mismatched image.
The legacy builder corrupts a layer. Do not remove that flag.

rules.rule: If you raise Node, revalidate Quartz BEFORE chasing a newer CLI
rules.why: The order is the whole point of the wrangler pin. #640 did the first half: the image's Node is 22 and Quartz v4.5.0 was revalidated on it; #675 did the second for Windows' runtime, so the CLI may now move, as its own piece.

whyWranglerAtAll: Cloudflare's upload protocol — BLAKE3 hashing, short-lived JWT, batched uploads — is undocumented enough that reimplementing it would break teachers' publishing whenever Cloudflare changed it. So the image carries their CLI instead.

recipeFolders.note: The recipe's FOLDERS, as data, because there were four hand-maintained copies of this list and they drifted the moment a fifth folder was added: the mac's WorkspaceModel.refreshToolchain, Windows' ToolchainMirror.RecipeFolders, the marketing screenshot harness (website/shots/capture.py), and the Dockerfile. Six carriers are pinned against this list in total, the other two being mac-app/project.yml and windows-app/Plantoir/Plantoir.csproj, which bundle and ship the folders; the Dockerfile is pinned in BOTH directions, since a COPY the contract does not list reproduces the original failure exactly. capture.py's own docstring said 'keep them in step' and it was the one that did not — which broke the demo workspace outright rather than subtly, because it copies the Dockerfile that expects the folder it did not copy.
recipeFolders.why: A .toolchain/ holding the new Dockerfile without the new folder is not stale, it is UNBUILDABLE: `docker buildx build` fails on the missing COPY, and preview.sh's friendly 'missing the build recipe' message cannot fire because the Dockerfile is present.

swiftImage.note: #493: the SECOND image, which compiles a course's ```swift run blocks to WebAssembly (shared-rules.json -> codeRunnerBlocks.swift). A top-level key of its own, deliberately NOT under `pins`: both apps' pin tests read every pin as a line the ROOT Dockerfile must contain, and these are lines of support/swift/Dockerfile, which is not the website builder's recipe. scripts/test_swift_blocks.py checks every `recipeContains` against support/swift/Dockerfile (Python, so Windows runs it too). Built by the launcher on the host - never by the build, which runs in the main container and cannot start another - the first time a preview has a block to compile; a teacher who never writes Swift never downloads it.
swiftImage.tag: teaching-quartz-swift:src-<first 8 hex of the launchers' toolchain_hash over support/swift ONLY>: a script edit elsewhere never rebuilds a 2 GB image, and an edit here changes this tag AND the website builder's (support/ is in its recipe), which costs a small rebuild of that one. prune_superseded_images has a twin for this prefix, by the same rules (never a blanket prune; nothing a container uses; nothing built in the last day).
swiftImage.measured: 2026-10-17, Colima on an Apple M4 Pro (arm64, 6 CPUs): 80 s to build with the downloads (about 1.30 GB: the toolchain 1,102,526,016 B, the SDK 92,760,992 B, binaryen 105,577,739 B); 2.24 GB on disk, 504 MB compressed, against 5.61 GB untrimmed (spike). The trim removes lldb, sourcekit, the package manager, the docs and the Linux host's own standard libraries in the same step that unpacks the toolchain. Every swift-gate/ fragment compiles to programs of exactly the sizes the untrimmed macOS toolchain makes (they differ only in the 16-byte module hash, which names the host: spike G4), and the same code compiles to the same bytes in every run of one image (verify.sh checks it); the table is in documentation/02-docker-image.md. x86_64 is pinned (downloaded once to take its SHA-256 and check its signature: toolchain 1,122,646,127 B, binaryen 111,200,018 B) but its compiles are not measured.

pins.why: The website builder's own base (Debian 13), so the first layer is shared and the Debian 13 toolchain's libraries are the system's.

The toolchain Phase 0 measured (6.4.0). GPG signature verified against the Swift 6.x Release Signing Key 52BB7E3DE28A71BE22EC05FFEF80A866B47A981F (spike, 2026-10-16). 6.4.1 (2026-10-12) is not taken: a toolchain move must re-run the swift-gate fragments, because Embedded Swift's surface changes between releases.

Review S7: Plantoir supports Intel Macs, and an arm64-only image would leave every Swift block not ready on one for ever. Chosen by TARGETARCH. Downloaded once to take this SHA-256; GPG signature verified (2026-10-17). Compiling on x86_64 is not measured.

ONE bundle for both host architectures (releases.json lists one checksum; it holds headers, modules and wasm libraries, no host programs), carrying the Embedded and the full SDK. Fetched with curl, checked with sha256sum and installed from the local file: `swift sdk install <url>` crashes on Linux 6.4.0 after its download (spike G1).
wasm-opt only (static; 17 MB kept), the version Phase 0 measured. OFF PATH: clang runs any wasm-opt on PATH by itself (Phase 0 trap 1). Matches GitHub's asset digest.
Review S7, as the toolchain. Matches GitHub's asset digest (2026-10-17).

swiftImage.rejected: The toolchain in the website builder's image (every teacher would download 1.3 GB for a language most never use); a Docker socket in the main container so the build could start this one (a container that can start containers can do anything on the Mac); SwiftPM per block (about 1 s more each, Phase 0); one module per course with every block an entry point (Path B: the full library is 0.9 MB brotli per block, not the 17 MB once feared, and Path B would rewrite top-level code into functions, changing what `main.swift` means); a hand-bumped version in the cache key instead of hashing the recipe (#485's reason).

swiftWindows.note: #570, v1.8.6: what Windows fetches to compile a course's ```swift run blocks (shared-rules.json -> codeRunnerBlocks.swift.windows), the counterpart of the mac's swiftImage. A top-level key of its own, NOT under `pins`, for swiftImage's reason: both apps' pin tests read every pin as a line of the root Dockerfile. Windows has no container (since 2026-08-19), so there is no image: preview.ps1 runs scripts/swift_windows_fetch.py, in the foreground as the mac builds its image, the first time a preview has a block to compile. It downloads the swift.org Windows installer, checks it, takes out only the compiler and its runtime without administrator rights, and keeps about 0.9 GB under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Plantoir\swift\6.4.0. A teacher who never writes Swift never downloads it. scripts/test_swift_windows.py reads every value here.
swiftWindows.configurationWhy: The bundle installs the ASSERTS toolchain by default (OptionsInstallAssertsToolchain = 1). noasserts (bld.noasserts) is the release configuration, the one closest to the Linux tarball the mac's image carries; every swift-gate fragment compiled with it to exactly the mac's sizes (2026-10-22). The asserts build was not measured.

installer.why: The ONLY Windows artifact swift.org publishes (releases.json lists no Windows checksum; .zip, .exe.sig and .msi all answer 404 - probed 2026-10-22), so the SHA-256 here, taken from the file itself, is the check that matters; the Authenticode signature (Apple Inc.) is defence in depth, the one signature Windows has (there is no GPG .sig). The bundle's payloads sit in ONE solid LZX cabinet attached at containerOffset: 'MSCF' there, cbCabinet = cabinetBytes, 33 files, and offset + cabinetBytes ends 10,622 bytes before the end of the file (the signature). /layout copies only installer.exe, and an HTTP Range fetch of just the payloads cannot be decoded (a solid folder: measured MISMATCH for all four), so the 2.1 GB download is unavoidable.

swiftWindows.payloadsWhy: The compiler, clang and wasm-ld (bld.noasserts) and the Swift runtime DLLs with the VC++ runtime (rtl.amd64), by their ids in the attached cabinet. The SHA-512s are Apple's own, from the bundle's Burn manifest (Payload/@Hash), so a payload that is not the one Apple built is refused. Each is taken out with Windows' own expand.exe -F:<id> and installed into a folder with `msiexec /a <msi> TARGETDIR=<dir> /qn`, an administrative extraction that needs no elevation (measured: exit 0, no UAC, not elevated).
swiftWindows.wasmSdkWhy: The SAME artifact bundle as the mac's image, by its pin (one url, one SHA-256), unpacked with Windows' own tar.exe. `swift sdk install` is NOT used: it needs MSVC's link.exe (Visual Studio) and a side-by-side folder only the IDE MSI carries (measured), and installing is only unpacking.

binaryen.why: wasm-opt only (10,343,424 B, fully static: KERNEL32 and SHELL32), the mac's version. Kept OUTSIDE the compiler's bin, because clang runs any wasm-opt it finds on PATH (Phase 0 trap 1). Matches GitHub's asset digest. arm64-windows exists and is not pinned: Plantoir for Windows is win-x64 only.

trim.why: Measured 2026-10-22: the extracted noasserts toolchain is 1,874,323,927 B; with the host libraries, headers, docs, duplicate executables and llvm-* tools removed it is 533,227,801 B and compiles every swift-gate fragment to the same bytes. The tools load VCRUNTIME140, VCRUNTIME140_1 and MSVCP140, which a PC without the VC++ redistributable lacks, so the rtl MSI's copies are put beside them. usr/lib/clang/<v>/include stays: clang needs it for FlushBeforeRead.c.

swiftWindows.keptBytesWhy: toolchain 533,231,069 + SDK 354,685,593 + wasm-opt 10,343,424, as the product's fetch keeps them (2026-10-22, READY.json). The measurement's hand trim was 3,268 B smaller: it also removed usr/bin/clang-deps-launcher.py, a Python script nothing here runs, which trim.remove does not name. Not part of the install digest, so a re-measured size never fetches again. Uninstalling Plantoir leaves it in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Plantoir\swift, as it leaves the assistant's models.
swiftWindows.measured: 2026-10-22, Lenovo 20QES70500 (Intel i5-8365U, 4 cores / 8 threads, 16 GB, Windows 11 Pro 26200, Ethernet), not elevated: the installer downloaded in 24.2 s in the measurement (about 87 MB/s) and the product's whole 2.3 GB in 21.5 s in its own first run (about 100 MB/s; a 50 Mbit/s school line would take about 6 min); everything after the download took about 142 s in that run (hashes and signature 40.1 s, expand 31.3 s, msiexec and trim 56.0 s, SDK 7.6 s, smoke 6.8 s), 104 s in the resumed one; the peak on disk was 4.82 GB (sampled every 2 s); all 15 swift-gate fragments compile to the mac's exact sizes and pass wasi_run.mjs; the compiled block runs in headless Edge 155 (swift_runner.mjs unmodified). The product path's own first-fetch timings are in documentation/12-windows-app.md.
swiftWindows.rejected: Carrying Swift in the installer (0.9 GB for every teacher, most of whom never write Swift); `swift sdk install` (needs Visual Studio's link.exe); installer.exe /layout (copies only itself); HTTP Range for just the needed payloads (one solid LZX folder); the asserts toolchain (the bundle's default, larger, not measured); WiX's `wix burn extract` (a .NET tool to ship, where expand.exe is part of Windows); cabinet.dll FDI in-process to avoid carving the cabinet out (the next step if the 4.82 GB peak ever matters); a container or WSL2 (Windows has had neither since 2026-08-19).

windowsPython.note: #764 (Windows 1.9.3): the Python in Windows' native runtime (runtime\python), the one base piece that does NOT mirror the image. A top-level key of its own, deliberately NOT under `pins`: the mac's pin test fails on a pin it does not know how to find in the Dockerfile, and this is not a Dockerfile line. Read only by the Windows suite (RuntimePythonTests: fetch-runtime.ps1 carries `windowsRuntimeContains`, Plantoir.csproj refuses a runtime on another Python, and a fetched runtime reports this version and an OpenSSL at least `opensslAtLeast`). The wheels' versions stay in `pins` (pythonFrontmatter, pyyaml, pillow); their hashes are fetch-runtime.ps1's own, as the Node zip's is.
windowsPython.why: Python's own OpenSSL is the TLS under every Netlify publish and deploy.py's Cloudflare API calls on Windows (Node's, which wrangler uses, is separate and is 3.5.9 with Node 22.23.4). The runtime carried Python 3.11.9, the last 3.11 with Windows binaries, whose OpenSSL is 3.0.13 (30 Jan 2024); OpenSSL 3.0 is out of public support (its last public release is 3.0.22, 25 Aug 2026; about 44 CVEs were fixed in 3.0.x after 3.0.13), and no 3.11 patch release can move it. 3.14.10 is the newest line with all three of: an OpenSSL in support (3.5.9, the 3.5 LTS, supported to 2030-04-08), Windows binary releases still coming (3.14 is in bugfix until about 2027-10, so the next OpenSSL fix arrives as a 3.14.x), and a win_amd64 wheel for every Python pin at the image's version. The image stays on python:3.11-slim (3.11.15, Debian's libssl3t64 >= 3.5.7 under the libssl3t64 pin), so the shared scripts/ must keep running on 3.11 and on 3.14: RuntimePythonTests.TheSharedScriptsParseAsPython311 parses every scripts/ and support/ file with feature_version 3.11 on Windows (it cannot see PEP 701 quote reuse in f-strings or stdlib functions added after 3.11), and PythonToolchainTests runs the shared tests on the runtime's 3.14. BEFORE 3.14 enters security-only (about 2027-10) the runtime must move again, to a line that still has Windows binaries, or this returns; that needs a PyYAML wheel for it.
windowsPython.measured: 2026-11-11, Lenovo 20QES70500 (i5-8365U, Windows 11 Pro 26200): each python.org embeddable amd64 zip checked against its published hash and run with -I. ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION: 3.11.9 'OpenSSL 3.0.13 30 Jan 2024'; 3.12.10 'OpenSSL 3.0.16 11 Feb 2025'; 3.13.17, 3.14.10 and 3.15.2 'OpenSSL 3.5.9 29 Sep 2026' (each tag's PCbuild/get_externals.bat agrees). 3.13.18 (2026-10-25) and 3.12.11 onwards are source-only. pip --only-binary on 3.15.2: no PyYAML 6.0.3 wheel. On 3.14.10 against 3.11.9, identical: libyaml, YAML 1.1 readings of no/off/yes/on, Pillow's freetype/webp/jpeg/zlib (raqm absent on both), 37 certificates in the default context, TLS to api.netlify.com and api.cloudflare.com, zoneinfo absent on both; all 93 scripts/test_*.py pass on both through PythonToolchainTests' shim; 140 .py files compile with no SyntaxWarning. The embed zip is 12,619,664 bytes (3.11.9's 11,249,023); its python.exe, python314.dll and libssl-3.dll are Authenticode-signed by the Python Software Foundation.
windowsPython.rejected: 3.13.17 (OpenSSL 3.5.9 today, but 3.13 went source-only four days later, so the next OpenSSL CVE returns us to #764); 3.12.10 (OpenSSL 3.0.16); 3.15.2 (no PyYAML 6.0.3 wheel, and PyYAML is the pin that decides what `publish: no` means; a .0 line a month old); python-build-standalone 3.11.18 (OpenSSL 3.5.9 and the image's minor, but a third-party builder, unsigned binaries, 49 MB download and 156 MB unpacked against 12.6 MB and 56 MB, a different layout); routing deploy.py's HTTP through Node (rewrites the shared publishing path on both platforms for one platform's packaging, and Python would still carry 3.0.13 for its other TLS); staying and documenting (the owner's ruling, 2026-11-10: fix it in 1.9.3); moving the image to 3.14 as well (its OpenSSL is current, and a base bump rebuilds every Mac). The FALLBACK, measured and kept for an emergency: 3.14.10's libssl-3.dll and libcrypto-3.dll copied into 3.11.9 report 'OpenSSL 3.5.9 29 Sep 2026' and complete TLS to Netlify (OpenSSL 3.x keeps its ABI) - not chosen because python.org never built or tested that pairing and 3.11.9 stays nine releases behind on CPython's own security fixes.

npmAudit.note: #667 (v1.9.0): what `npm audit` reports against the image's JavaScript, and which findings are accepted and why. verify.sh audits every tree below inside the image, with the image's own npm, and FAILS on a high or critical advisory that is not accepted here for that tree, or that is accepted at a LOWER severity than the database gives it now (re-decide). Low and moderate advisories that are not accepted are reported, not failed; an accepted advisory no longer reported is stale, said and not failed. Offline it SKIPS, saying no tree counts as audited until every tree can be. A top-level key, deliberately NOT under `pins`: both apps' pin tests read every pin as a Dockerfile line. Every current advisory is listed, low and moderate included, with the severity it has today, so a later raise fails. `exposure` and `reason` are decided per tree, because one advisory can be harmless in one tree and not in another. Windows audits its runtime's copies of the same trees (`windowsRuntime`) against this same list. scripts/npm_audit.py is the comparator; research/npm-audit/<date>.md is the record of each run; RELEASING.md step 2 revisits it at every cut. REJECTED: upgrading now (the ruling on #667: no upgrades this release; Quartz's tree moves with Quartz 5, #512, and wrangler's moved with its own piece, #699, whose 4.156.0 has no advisory, so wrangler has no accepted entry today); `npm audit --audit-level=high` alone, which cannot say 'accepted', so every run would be red; auditing in the image build, which would need the network on every build and fail a teacher's first build the day an advisory is published.

trees.exposure: Quartz v4.5.0 and every dependency its lockfile installs, dev dependencies included. Runs in the container on the teacher's Mac: the build, and the preview server while a preview runs. A built site carries Quartz's own client scripts and stylesheets.
node-tikzjax and its locked dependencies (support/figures/package-lock.json, npm ci --omit=dev). Build only: a site carries the SVG it draws, never the engine.

abcjs and linkedom and their locked dependencies (support/music/package-lock.json, npm ci --omit=dev, #679). abcjs draws at build time and its one prebuilt file, abcjs-basic-min.js, runs in the student's browser on a press of Play; linkedom is build only.

Cloudflare's deploy command line, a global install that keeps no lockfile: one is built from the installed tree (npm install --package-lock-only next to a copy of it). Runs only during a Cloudflare deploy.

A prebuilt file a site carries for printing: it runs in the student's browser. Its lockfile is built from the pin's version, so an advisory against pagedjs itself is caught exactly, and its bundled dependencies only as they resolve today.
A prebuilt file a site carries for graphs: it runs in the student's browser. Its lockfile is built from the pin's version, with the same limit as pagedjs.

accepted.reason: Installed with pixi.js for Quartz's Graph view, which build_site.py removes (the remove-Graph patch), so nothing calls it at build time and a built site carries neither pixi nor xmldom (measured 2026-10-24 on a built ICS4U site: no 'pixi' or 'xmldom' in prescript.js or postscript.js). Fixing it means moving Quartz's own lockfile, which waits for Quartz 5 (#512).

accepted.exposure: the teacher's build, and the preview server on the teacher's Mac
accepted.reason: Denial of service on crafted brace patterns, under minimatch (Quartz's globs, rimraf, and serve-handler in the preview server). The patterns are Quartz's and serve-handler's own, never a teacher's notes or a student's request.
An infinite loop on a malformed ZIP64 archive. fflate is under satori and opentype.js, reading the fonts the image carries.

The advisory is the glob COMMAND LINE's -c/--cmd option. Quartz reaches glob as a library through rimraf and never runs its command line. GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 (moderate, published after 2026-10-28) is glob 9 to 14.0.1 carrying on through the filesystem after an AbortSignal has cancelled it: Quartz's one call is `rimraf(path.join(output, "*"), { glob: true, ... })` in its build.ts, with no signal, so there is nothing to cancel (read 2026-10-31 in the image: rimraf 6.0.1 passes a signal to glob only when its caller gave one).
Inside Sass (esbuild-sass-plugin). Sass compiles Quartz's and Plantoir's own stylesheets, never a teacher's or a student's input.
CPU denial of service or prototype pollution from crafted YAML (gray-matter, Quartz, rehype-citation). The YAML is the teacher's own front matter, in a build on their own Mac.
Needs an existing prototype pollution to bypass KaTeX's trust settings. Quartz renders the maths at build time; a site carries KaTeX's stylesheet, fonts and copy-tex (#494), not the renderer.

accepted.exposure: its output reaches the student's browser, from the teacher's input
accepted.reason: An unsanitised class attribute from Markdown. Only the teacher writes the Markdown a site is built from. Moderate, so not gated; recorded so a raise to high fails.

accepted.exposure: the teacher's build, and the preview server on the teacher's Mac
accepted.reason: ReDoS on crafted glob patterns. The patterns are Quartz's and serve-handler's own, never a teacher's notes or a student's request. GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (moderate, published after 2026-10-28) is the same shape, a denial of service from a crafted pattern's expansion: the patterns are still Quartz's own ignorePatterns (build.ts) and serve-handler's own configuration, so it is accepted on the same reason.
ReDoS and wrong matches on crafted glob patterns (globby, fast-glob, micromatch). The patterns are Quartz's own.

Improper escaping in the SVG satori generates. Quartz uses satori only in its CustomOgImages emitter (social-preview images), and build_site.py comments that emitter out of quartz.config.ts on every build unless --include-social-media-previews is passed, which neither app passes (contracts/app-rules.json lists it among the flags the apps do not pass). With the flag, what satori draws is the teacher's own page titles and course name, and its SVG goes straight to sharp to become a PNG, so no generated SVG reaches a site. Checked 2026-10-28: build_site.py's toggle_custom_og_images, and the Windows runtime's quartz.config.ts (the same Quartz v4.5.0 file the image carries) naming Plugin.CustomOgImages() for it to comment out.
libvips, libheif and librsvg issues with hostile images. sharp here renders Quartz's own generated social-preview images, not uploaded ones.
Inside Sass, over the source maps of Quartz's and Plantoir's own stylesheets.
Recursion, CPU denial of service or prototype pollution from crafted TOML (Quartz's +++ front matter). The TOML is the teacher's own, in a build on their own Mac.

accepted.reason: Quartz's live-reload server while a preview runs (--serve --wsPort): a memory-exhaustion denial of service, and memory disclosure, of the preview's own websocket. A built site carries no ws. The preview ports listen beyond localhost today, which is its own finding.
